newsitem.title: DENMARK: BADMINTON-OLYMPIC CHAMPION HOYER-LARSEN BEATEN ON HOME GROUND.
newsitem.headline: BADMINTON-OLYMPIC CHAMPION HOYER-LARSEN BEATEN ON HOME GROUND.

text.p: Olympic badminton champion Poul-Erik Hoyer-Larsen failed on Saturday in his bid to win the Danish Open for the fourth year running, losing in three games to Malaysian Ong Ewe Hock in the semifinals.
Ong won 15-7 7-15 15-9 with Hoyer-Larsen telling reporters later: "I never got to open (out) the game and it was Ong who was in control for a large part of the contest.
"In the first game I held back a little too much and in the third I was over-eager and made it too easy for him."

Hoyer-Larsen plays in the German Open next week but then plans to stay out of tournaments while he gets into shape for the Grand Prix finals in December with an eye also on the 1997 world championships in Scotland.
In Sunday's final, Ong faces another top Dane in Thomas Stuer-Lauridsen who beat compatriot Peter Gade 5-15 15-6 17-14.
The women's final will be between two unseeded players -- Sweden's Marina Andrievskaya and Gong Zhichao of China.
